display.purpose: Hero headline only; the city profile name shares the voice. Uppercase, wdth 125, balanced wrap.

headline.purpose: Section titles and the data nameplate title. Uppercase, wdth 125.

title.purpose: Leader strip heading, results heading, city plate, map readout name, lamp caption. Uppercase, wdth 118-125.

label.purpose: Uppercase tracked labels: table headers, gauge titles, legend headings, nameplate terms.

shadows.name: lift
shadows.purpose: Default for anything sitting on a panel: buttons, fields, keys, readouts, legends, tooltips, toast.

shadows.name: face
shadows.purpose: Enamel dial faces, ranking table, results board.

shadows.name: key-lip
shadows.purpose: Resting bevel on filled buttons; white keys and toggles use inset 0 -5px 0 #D8DBD4.

shadows.name: pressed
shadows.purpose: Checked keys, toggled-on controls, active presets (.45 on button :active).

shadows.name: housing
shadows.purpose: Black gauge cluster and mixer housings.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: All UI transitions (buttons 150ms, nav 200ms, leader hover 200ms, toast 350ms). No overshoot.

motion.name: ease-knob
motion.purpose: Knob rotation 500ms, edge-scale needle 700ms, result bars 600ms, order toggle 350ms, map dot radius 250ms. No overshoot.

motion.name: needle-spring
motion.value: stiffness 150, damping 13, 4 substeps/frame, dt capped at 34ms, settle at |v|,|x| < 0.04deg
motion.purpose: The only overshoot in the system: dial needles swing slightly underdamped. Stagger 70-110ms across clusters. Snaps under prefers-reduced-motion.

dialGeometry.ticks: 41 ticks; every 4th major (len 12, w 1.8), every 2nd mid (len 7), minor (len 4, w 1)

narrative.overview:
Miastometr is a measuring instrument, not a comparison site. Every city is read off a white enamel dial with black ticks and a red / mustard / green scale band, housed in signal-orange, teal and mustard bakelite panels joined by black seams. The reference world is 1970s Polish lab and switchboard hardware (ERA, Meratronik): rotary selector knobs, piano-key switches, faders, indicator lamps and engraved nameplates. The UI borrows their physical grammar: things are pressed, turned and read, and the needle does the talking.

The palette is committed and saturated at the panel scale, but each instrument face stays white and quiet so readings stay legible. Type is a single variable family, Archivo, stretched from expanded placard caps (wdth 125) for headings down to plain width for body and condensed tabular numerals for readings. Density is medium: generous panel padding, compact instruments.

The system is light only, by explicit user request. There are no dark-mode tokens and `color-scheme` is pinned to light. The rejected look is the category's blue card-grid dashboard.
keyCharacteristics: Full-bleed color panels, alternating orange / enamel / teal / white / mustard / enamel, separated by 3px black seams.
White enamel dial faces inside a single black bezel; needles that swing on a spring.
Archivo from wdth 125 uppercase placards to tabular-numeral readouts.
Physical controls: rotary knob, piano keys, faders, indicator lamps.
Tactile depth: inset bottom lips on keys and buttons, soft drop shadows under housings, never flat cards.

rules.name: The Three-Zone Rule
rules.body: Zone red and zone green appear only as the outer thirds of the scale band (split at 33.3% / 66.6%) and the colors derived from it (map dots, legend, the comparison winner dot). Mustard is also a panel and signal color, but on a white face it always means the middle zone.

rules.name: The Neutral Size Rule
rules.body: Population is not better or worse. Its dials carry a solid black band at 80% opacity instead of zones, and its map dots are white.

rules.name: The Lamp Rule
rules.body: Air quality is categorical, so it is shown as an indicator lamp in the GIOŚ category color, never as a percentile needle. When air quality is selected the hero dial fades to 16% and a lamp replaces it; the lamp scale uses the six GIOŚ levels from very good to very bad.

rules.name: The Three Needles Rule
rules.body: Comparisons use orange, teal and black needles in that order, and the same three colors mark each city's chip everywhere in the compare view.

rules.name: The Tabular Reading Rule
rules.body: Every number that can change (table cells, readouts, values, tick numerals) uses tabular numerals so needles and columns don't jitter.

rules.name: The Width Axis Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy is carried by width and weight together: wdth 125 for placards, 108–118 for titles and readings, 100 for body. Don't substitute a second family.

rules.name: The Press-In Rule
rules.body: A control that is on is pushed in (inset shadow, black fill), never raised or glowing. Hover lifts by 1–3px at most.

rules.name: The One Bezel Rule
rules.body: Each instrument has exactly one black frame. A dial inside a leader tile, gauge or compare card loses its own border and shadow; the tile or the black cluster is the bezel. Never nest a bordered card in a bordered card.

dos: Do alternate full-bleed panels in the order orange, enamel, teal, white, mustard, enamel, joined by 3px black seams (`3px solid #1C1C1A`).
Do put numerals outside the zone band so needles sweep only over ticks.
Do give every instrument exactly one black bezel, and strip borders and shadows from dials nested inside it.

Do use the ease-out curves only in CSS (`cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1)` for UI, `cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1)` for knob and needle-like slides). The only overshoot in the system is the JS needle spring (stiffness 150, damping 13).
Do show air quality as an indicator lamp in the GIOŚ category color.
Do keep population dials neutral: a black band, no zones, white map dots.
Do use tabular numerals for every reading and a black 3px focus outline (white on orange and teal panels).
Do set black text on signal orange and mustard, and white text on teal and black.
donts: Don't add dark-mode tokens or a dark theme; the system is light only by user request.
Don't drive a percentile needle for air quality.
Don't use zone red or zone green outside the scale band and its derived map, legend and winner marks.
Don't nest a bordered card inside a bordered card.
Don't add bouncy or overshooting CSS easing; overshoot belongs to the needle spring alone.
Don't put eyebrows or kickers above headings; a section opens with its uppercase title.
Don't use a second typeface; widen or condense Archivo instead.
Don't fall back to the blue card-grid dashboard look of comparison sites.
